ledger.claim: The route deviation is established on this trip's own trace. The gps_trace records trace_distance_km of 24.6 km against a booked optimal_distance_km of 19.6 km, an excess of 5.0 km or 25.51% of optimal. Both limbs of the POL-RD-01 gate pass: the excess is greater than 20% of optimal and greater than 0.8 km absolute. POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure the governing measurement, so trip_record.actual_distance_km is not relied on for the threshold test.

The trace is clean for policy purposes, so the deviation needs no corroboration. Under POL-RD-07 the trace is impaired only by a gap above 90 seconds, a straight-line jump above 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval above 30 seconds. This trace has coverage_pct 100.0, an empty gaps array, max_gap_sec 0.0 and a 10 second sample interval across 205 fixes, so none of the three limbs fires. The admissibility pre-pass also tags this artifact COMPLETE at weight 1.0 with no issues.

The driver's explanation - a CTE queue at the Braddell exit - fails. It is asserted in his counterparty_statement but names no evidence ID, and the only advisory artifact in this bundle is ABSENT: EV-ADVIS-00508-01 carries status MISSING, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, with no payload, so it can carry no fact. POL-RD-03 cannot be run without an advisory that names a road the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the time the trace shows the vehicle reaching that segment. POL-RD-13 provides that such an assertion is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else, that where the bundle holds none the comparison cannot be run and POL-RD-03 is unavailable, and that the assertion therefore carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The deviation stands at the measured figure and no amended optimal is supplied.

No other exculpatory clause is available on this record, so nothing reduces the 5.0 km excess before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 are applied. POL-RD-04 requires a rider instruction recorded in the chat_log; the chat export for this trip holds zero messages (message_count 0, empty messages array), so no rider-requested detour or added stop exists. POL-RD-05 requires an amended pickup or dropoff; both pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and both amended_optimal_distance_km and amended_optimal_duration_min are null, so there is no re-quote to run. POL-RD-12 is confined to RYDE_POOL trips and this trip's vehicle_type is RYDE_TAXI.

The refund is arithmetic under POL-RD-02, not discretionary. The fare_breakdown shows fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply and the distance and time lines are recomputable on the booked optimal route: ((3.80 base + 0.75 x 19.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 26.0 optimal min) x surge 1.0) + 0.80 platform fee, with no ERP or toll lines, no fixed surcharge and no waiting-time fee, giving a recomputed_fare of 26.58. Refund = charged_total 32.57 - 26.58 = 5.99, which is above the 0.50 de minimis floor and below the 90% full-refund share (it is 18.39% of charged_total), and rounds UP to SGD 6.00.

The driver's point that the rider's usual price depends on time of day does not assist him. The surge_multiplier recorded on the fare_breakdown for this trip is 1.0, and the POL-RD-02 recomputation runs on the same stored rate card that produced the charged total - base fare 3.80, 0.75 per km, 0.28 per minute, 0.80 platform fee. The refund is computed from this trip's own fare_breakdown, so a memory of past prices is neither the benchmark nor a defence.

The rider's initial burden under POL-RD-08 is discharged on the cited artifacts: trip_record, gps_trace and fare_breakdown all carry trip_id TRP-00508, the trace first fix at 08:21:40 matches the trip_record started_at, and the excess is measured from a trace that is not impaired under POL-RD-07. The supplemental corroboration condition in POL-RD-08 is not engaged: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 0 and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d_substantiated is 0, so the four-or-more trigger is not met and the gps_trace alone carries the threshold finding. The driver, by contrast, points to no artifact and no clause that reduces the excess.

The rider is presently carrying the whole disputed charge: the fare_breakdown shows payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.0 against a charged total of 32.57. Under POL-GEN-03 a NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute leaves the payment state exactly as it is, which on these facts means the rider stays out of pocket. Only a refund moves the money back to the filing party, and the rider's case is made out on this trip's own unimpaired trace.

The trace-governed excess on this trip is 5.0 km over the booked optimal of 19.6 km, or 25.51%. That clears POL-RD-01's establishment gate (more than 20% and more than 0.8 km) but falls a long way short of its materiality gate of more than 50% of optimal or more than 8.0 km absolute. No MATERIAL deviation is recorded, so the material-deviation regime in POL-RD-06 — the only route to a FULL refund on rider-side evidence — is not engaged, and the driver's liability is bounded by the ordinary POL-RD-02 recomputation.

The whole of the driver's monetary exposure is fixed by POL-RD-02's arithmetic, run on the fare_breakdown itself: recomputed_fare = (3.80 base + 0.75 x 19.6 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = 26.58, against a charged_total of 32.57, giving a refund of 5.99 rounded up to SGD 6.00. The fare model is METERED, so POL-RD-02 and not POL-RD-11 supplies the remedy, and the rider's claim to the full SGD 32.57 she has contested is unsupported on the platform's own arithmetic.

The computed refund is 18.4% of charged_total, nowhere near the 90% share POL-RD-02 requires before FULL_REFUND displaces the partial, and it is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis so it does not collapse to no action either. The only outcome the arithmetic supports is a bounded PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.00 — not the complete reversal the rider seeks.

Every dollar on the receipt is meter arithmetic on the route actually driven: 3.80 base fare, 18.45 distance (24.6 km x 0.75), 9.52 time (34.0 min x 0.28) and 0.80 platform fee, with surge_multiplier 1.0 read from the fare_breakdown, zero ERP lines, no airport surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo. There is no unmatched or phantom charge line, no billing-integrity failure under POL-RD-09, and nothing on the receipt sustains the rider's 'ripping people off' characterisation beyond the 5.0 km of established excess itself.

Any repeat-deviation uplift is foreclosed on the driver's own record: driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against driver_profile.completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern is ESTABLISHED under POL-RD-06 and neither the deterrent FULL_REFUND uplift in limb (b) nor the conduct referral in limb (c) can attach. POL-GEN-01 confines that profile to that named test, and no other field on it may carry any finding against the driver.

The driver's explanation of a CTE queue at the Braddell exit is tested against the traffic_advisory for this trip and nothing else. EV-ADVIS-00508-01 is MISSING — issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload and no validity window — so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. The driver cited no advisory identifier, so the absence is a gap in the bundle and not a clause invoked against a cited artifact; under POL-RD-13 that gap does not engage POL-RD-10(5). The consequence is a ruling on the measured excess with the ordinary POL-RD-02 refund, not an escalation and not an enlargement of the excess.

The rider's account — 'same route every time, never above 40' and a referral to the authorities — is narrative with no artifact behind it: the trip's chat log is empty (message_count 0) and no admissible document records any usual-price benchmark. POL-RD-02 makes the refund arithmetic rather than discretionary and POL-RD-08 gives no weight to assertions that cite no evidence ID, so this trip is priced from its own trace and its own booked optimal, and nothing entitles the rider to more than the SGD 6.00 that arithmetic produces.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a rider-filed route-deviation dispute over trip TRP-00508 (Woodlands MRT to Novena Square, 27 Aug 2026), charged SGD 32.57.

FINDING. The deviation is established on the trace. Under POL-RD-01 the traced distance is 24.6 km (EV-GPS-00508, the governing figure; trip_record.actual_distance_km is only a rounded copy of the same measurement) against a booked optimal of 19.6 km (EV-TRIP-00508): an excess of 5.0 km, or 25.51% of optimal. Both limbs of the establishment gate pass (greater than 20% and greater than 0.8 km). It is NOT a MATERIAL deviation (neither above 50% nor above 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 repeat-pattern regime is not engaged; in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 0 against completed_trips_90d of 250, so no pattern exists and no driver-conduct referral attaches.

DRIVER'S EXPLANATION. The assertion of a CTE queue at the Braddell exit is tested against the traffic advisory for this trip and nothing else (POL-RD-13). EV-ADVIS-00508-01 is MISSING (issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight_multiplier 0.0, no payload, no validity window), so POL-RD-03 cannot be run on the record and the assertion carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Because the driver cited no advisory identifier, this is a gap in the bundle rather than an exculpatory clause invoked against a cited artifact, so POL-RD-10(5) is not engaged and the case is decided on the measured excess; no amended optimal is supplied. The further point that the rider's usual price depends on the time of day does not change the arithmetic, which runs on this trip's own fare_breakdown with surge_multiplier 1.0.

OTHER EXCULPATORY CLAUSES. POL-RD-04: the chat log for this trip holds zero messages (message_count 0), so there is no rider-requested detour or added stop. POL-RD-05: pickup_amended_at and dropoff_amended_at are null and no amended re-quote exists. POL-RD-12: the vehicle is RYDE_TAXI, not RYDE_POOL.

REFUND (POL-RD-02, fare_model METERED, so POL-RD-11 does not apply):
- charged_total: SGD 32.57
- recomputed_fare: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 19.6 km + 0.28 x 26.0 min) x 1.0 surge + 0.80 platform fee = SGD 26.58
- refund: 32.57 - 26.58 = SGD 5.99, rounded UP to SGD 6.00

The refund is above the SGD 0.50 de minimis and is 18.4% of charged_total, far below the 90% share that would make it a full refund, so the outcome is PARTIAL_REFUND of SGD 6.00.

BILLING. There is no ERP or toll charge on the receipt (on-optimal and off-optimal ERP totals both SGD 0.00) and no airport surcharge (the trip does not originate at an airport), so there is no phantom line and no billing-integrity correction or referral under POL-RD-09(4). The rider's request for the whole SGD 32.57 is not supported: the trace shows 5.0 km of excess, not a wholly wrong route, and the rider's account of a 'usual price' and of a report to the authorities has no artifact behind it.

CONFIDENCE. The deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-00508, EV-TRIP-00508 and EV-FARE-00508, each at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no admissibility issues; the trace is not impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07(a)-(c) (100% coverage, no gaps, max gap 0.0 s, 10 s sampling across 205 fixes), so no independent corroboration is required.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
